section.title: PortGroups npm and bun — Node.js and Bun
section.para: The npm and bun PortGroups install packages from the npm registry (registry.npmjs.org). npm uses npm install -g; bun installs from a local tarball with bun install --frozen-lockfile against a required bun.lock. Both fetch the same ${distname}${extract.suffix} tarball and expose its bin entries in ${prefix}/bin, but they differ in runtime, dependency pinning, and lifecycle-script trust. Ports that declare engines.bun or ship a #!/usr/bin/env bun shebang must use bun; the npm PortGroup wraps bins with Node and cannot run them. All other JavaScript CLIs should use npm.

listitem.para: npm — wraps bins with node, requires nodejs at runtime, runs lifecycle scripts via npm. Only the top-level tarball is checksummed; dependencies are fetched at destroot.

bun — native bun runtime (#!/usr/bin/env bun), destroots to ${prefix}/lib/bun/${name} with relative symlinks into ${prefix}/bin, so two bun ports can coexist. Requires ${filespath}/bun.lock (or bun.lockfile) and installs with --frozen-lockfile. Destroot still needs network to fetch lockfile-pinned deps; the lockfile pins the dependency graph.

section.title: PortGroup npm
section.para: Installs an npm package globally. The PortGroup imitates npm install -g by passing the fetched tarball directly (extract.only; no extraction) and installing with --global --prefix=${destroot}${prefix}.

section.title: Usage
section.programlisting:
PortSystem 1.0 PortGroup npm 1.0
name my-cli version 1.2.3 npm.rootname @scope/my-cli # defaults to ${name} if omitted
checksums rmd160 ... \ sha256 ... \ size ...

listitem.para: Npm package name, including scope if any (e.g. @scope/pkg). Defaults to ${name}. master_sites is https://registry.npmjs.org/${npm.rootname}/-/ and distname is ${npm.rootname}-${version}.
Type: optional, defaults to ${name}
Example: npm.rootname @babel/core
Node.js version to depend on. Maps to path:bin/node:nodejs${npm.nodejs_version} in depends_lib.
Type: optional
Default: 22
Example: npm.nodejs_version 20
npm version to depend on. Maps to path:bin/npm:npm${npm.version} in depends_build.
Type: optional
Default: 10
Example: npm.version 10

When yes (default), adds path:bin/node:nodejs${npm.nodejs_version} to depends_lib and path:bin/npm:npm${npm.version} to depends_build via port::register_callback. Disable only if the Portfile manages Node/npm deps manually.
Type: optional
Default: yes

Set from npm.rootname; extract.suffix .tgz, livecheck.url https://registry.npmjs.org/${npm.rootname}/latest with regex "version":"([^"]+)". Only the top-level tarball is checksummed; its dependencies are fetched at destroot.
use_configure no, build {}; destroot runs npm install --global --prefix=${destroot}${prefix} in ${workpath}.

section.title: PortGroup bun
section.para: Installs a package from the npm registry for CLIs that declare engines.bun and ship #!/usr/bin/env bun (the npm PortGroup wraps bins with Node and cannot run them). Destroot writes a private package.json that depends on the checksummed tarball as file:./…, copies bun.lockfile, and runs bun install --frozen-lockfile. Bins under node_modules/.bin that point into the packaged module are linked as relative symlinks into ${prefix}/bin.
Layout: ${prefix}/lib/bun/${name} with bins in ${prefix}/bin, so two bun ports can be active together. Cache at ${workpath}/.bun-cache.

section.title: Usage
section.programlisting:
PortSystem 1.0 PortGroup bun 1.0
name oh-my-pi version 18.12.6 bun.rootname @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent
checksums rmd160 ... \ sha256 ... \ size ...
# files/bun.lock is required (default bun.lockfile) # Generate once from the distfile: # cp ${distpath}/${distname}.tgz /tmp && cd /tmp # # package.json: { "dependencies": { "${bun.rootname}": "file:./${distname}.tgz" } } # bun install --lockfile-only && cp bun.lock ${filespath}/
# optional bun.version 1.3.0 bun.trusted_dependencies sharp esbuild bun.add_dependencies yes

listitem.para: Npm package name, including scope (e.g. @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent). Defaults to ${name}. master_sites is https://registry.npmjs.org/${bun.rootname}/-/, distname is [file tail ${bun.rootname}]-${version} (scoped prefix stripped; no need to set distname manually), extract.suffix .tgz. Livecheck mirrors npm: https://registry.npmjs.org/${bun.rootname}/latest.
Type: required if package name differs from ${name}
Example: bun.rootname @scope/pkg

Path to the bun.lock that pins the dependency graph for destroot. Must exist as a regular file or destroot fails with missing bun.lockfile. Ship it under files/ and regenerate when bumping version (or when upstream deps change).
From a fetched distfile:
listitem.programlisting: cp ${distpath}/${distname}.tgz /tmp && cd /tmp # write package.json: # { "dependencies": { "${bun.rootname}": "file:./${distname}.tgz" } } bun install --lockfile-only && cp bun.lock ${filespath}/

listitem.para: Type: optional path
Default: ${filespath}/bun.lock
Optional minimum bun runtime version (floor), checked at destroot against ${prefix}/bin/bun --version. Use to honor engines.bun.
Type: optional
Default: {} (no check)
Example: bun.version 1.3.0

List of dependency package names whose lifecycle scripts (postinstall, prepare, etc.) bun may run. Unlike npm, bun runs no lifecycle scripts unless the package is trusted. The PortGroup always writes trustedDependencies that replaces bun's default allowlist (bun only falls back to its built-in list when the field is absent) — deliberate so the set of scripts does not shift when devel/bun updates. Every dependency that needs a script, including ones a stock bun install would trust (e.g. sharp), must be listed here. Destroot runs with --verbose, so blocked scripts are named in the log.
The PortGroup always trusts ${bun.rootname} itself (local tarball installs require an explicit trust).
Type: optional
Default: {}
Example: bun.trusted_dependencies sharp esbuild
When yes (default), adds path:bin/bun:bun to depends_lib (the shebang is #!/usr/bin/env bun). Disable only if the Portfile manages the bun dependency manually.
Type: optional
Default: yes
extract.only — installing from the extract directory would symlink it, then extract removes it. use_configure no, build {}.

Creates ${prefix}/lib/bun/${name} and ${prefix}/bin, copies the distfile tarball and bun.lockfile, writes package.json with trustedDependencies and a file:./${distname}.tgz dependency on ${bun.rootname}, then:
Removes the copied tarball, then links each node_modules/.bin/* symlink whose target lies under the packaged module into ${prefix}/bin as ../lib/bun/${name}/…. Fails if ${prefix}/bin is empty.
Only the top-level tarball is checksummed; lockfile-pinned dependencies are fetched from registry.npmjs.org at destroot. Bump and regenerate files/bun.lock with the port version.
Relative bin symlinks are written, so destroot paths do not leak into the image.
For local testing: port lint and sudo port -vst install; bun --version should satisfy bun.version when set.
